Hello! My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you're here today, and I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've been through recently. Becoming a new mother can be a life-altering experience, and it's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential concerns. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it can help us have a more informed discussion about your postpartum experience.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm here to create a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a judgment, but rather an opportunity for us to work together to ensure you're receiving the care and support you need during this important time.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions, and we'll go through them together one by one. I'll ask you to share your thoughts and feelings, and I'll take note of your responses. This will help us get a better understanding of your postpartum experience and identify any areas where you might need additional support.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or struggling to cope?

.. I don't know, it's just been really tough lately. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but everything feels so overwhelming. I'm just so tired all the time, and I feel like I'm not doing anything right. I'm worried about the baby's health, and I feel like I'm constantly checking on her to make sure she's okay. It's like, I know it's normal to worry, but it feels like it's consuming me sometimes. 

As for enjoying things, I don't really have the energy for much of anything anymore. I used to love reading and taking walks, but now I just feel like I'm too exhausted to even think about those things. And when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, it just doesn't feel the same. It's like, I'll be sitting there, trying to read a book, and all I can think about is whether the baby is sleeping okay, or if I need to feed her soon. It's hard to focus on anything else.

I don't know, maybe I'm just not doing this mom thing right. Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, you know? But at the same time, I don't feel like I'm completely falling apart or anything. I just feel... stuck, I guess. Like, I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby, but I'm not really living my life anymore. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

To be honest, I haven't been laughing as much as I used to. I mean, I still smile and feel happy when my baby does something cute, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. I feel like I've been so focused on taking care of her and making sure everything is okay that I haven't had the energy to really enjoy the funny moments. And when I do try to laugh, it feels a little forced, you know? Like, I'll be watching a funny video or something, and I'll think, "Oh, that's hilarious," but I won't really feel it deep down.

Sometimes my husband will try to make me laugh, and it's nice, but it's just not the same as when we were laughing together before the baby was born. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a happy person, but I'm not really feeling it. And that's hard for me, because I've always been a pretty positive person, and it's weird to feel like that's missing right now.

I do have moments where I feel happy, though. Like, when my baby smiles at me, or when she falls asleep in my arms, that's just the best feeling in the world. But it's not like I'm feeling happy and laughing all the time. It's more like... occasional glimpses of happiness, I guess. Does that make sense?
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll think about something I want to do, like going for a walk or meeting a friend, and I'll get excited for a second, but then I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do to make it happen, like finding a babysitter or making sure the baby's fed and changed, and it just feels too overwhelming. So, I end up not doing it.

And even when I do have something to look forward to, like a visit from my mom or a postpartum support group, I'll get anxious about it instead of excited. I'll worry about whether the baby will be fussy, or if I'll be able to get everything ready on time. It's like, I'm just so focused on surviving each day that I'm not really thinking about the future or looking forward to things.

But, there are some things that I do look forward to, like my baby's bath time. I love giving her a bath and playing with her in the water. It's just so much fun, and it's one of the few times when I feel like I can really relax and enjoy her. And, sometimes, when my husband comes home from work, I'll look forward to that, because it means I'll have some help and some adult conversation. So, it's not like I never look forward to things, it's just... it's not as often as it used to be, and it's not as carefree.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I do that a lot, unfortunately. I feel like I'm constantly questioning myself and wondering if I'm doing everything right. If the baby is crying, I think, "What did I do wrong? Is she hungry? Is she tired? Is she uncomfortable?" And if I'm having a hard time getting her to latch or if she's not sleeping well, I feel like it's all my fault. Like, I'm not good enough or I'm not doing something right.

Even when things are going well, I'll sometimes think, "What if I'm just getting lucky? What if I'm not really cut out for this mom thing?" It's like, I'm always second-guessing myself and wondering if I'm making mistakes. And if something does go wrong, like if the baby gets a fever or if I forget to do something important, I'll beat myself up over it. I'll think, "How could I have been so stupid? Why didn't I remember that?"

It's hard for me to shake off the feeling that I'm not doing enough or that I'm not good enough. I feel like I'm just winging it most of the time, and that's a really scary feeling. My husband tries to reassure me and tell me that I'm doing a great job, but it's hard for me to believe him when I'm feeling so uncertain and insecure. Does that make sense?
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah... I'd say that's definitely been happening to me. I mean, I'm always worrying about something, even when everything seems fine. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll start thinking, "What if she's not getting enough milk? What if she's not gaining weight fast enough?" Or, I'll be putting her to sleep, and I'll start thinking, "What if she rolls over and gets stuck? What if she stops breathing?"

It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll get really anxious and worked up. And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my husband, too - like, what if he gets hurt on the way home from work? Or, I'll worry about our house - like, what if there's a fire or a break-in?

Sometimes, I'll be awake in the middle of the night, just lying there, worrying about everything and nothing at the same time. It's like, my brain just won't turn off, and I'll be thinking about all these things that could go wrong. And it's not even like I can control any of it, you know? It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety and worry that I don't know how to shake.

It's exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And even when everything is fine, I'll still find ways to worry about it. Like, I'll think, "Okay, everything is fine now, but what about tomorrow? What about next week?" It's just this never-ending cycle of anxiety and worry that I don't know how to break.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah... that's happened to me a few times, and it's really scary. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some huge emergency, but there's nothing actually wrong.

It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is just... overreacting, I guess. Like, I'll be thinking about something, and then suddenly I'll feel this intense fear or anxiety, and it's not even related to what I was thinking about. It's like, my brain just gets hijacked by this feeling of panic, and I don't know how to calm it down.

Sometimes, it happens when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll start thinking, "What if something happens to me? What if I'm not able to take care of her?" And then I'll start feeling this panic rising up, and I'll be like, "Okay, okay, calm down, everything is fine..." But it's hard to shake off that feeling of fear and anxiety.

It's not all the time, but it's happened enough that it's started to worry me. Like, I'll be thinking, "Is this normal? Am I just being paranoid?" But at the same time, it's hard to ignore that feeling of panic when it happens. It's like, my body is trying to tell me something, but I don't know what it is or how to listen to it.

It's funny, because my husband will sometimes notice when I'm feeling anxious or panicked, and he'll be like, "Hey, what's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know, I just feel... scared, I guess." And he'll try to calm me down, but it's hard to explain what's going on when I don't even understand it myself.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah... that's definitely been happening to me. I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, you know? With the baby and the sleep deprivation and the constant worrying... it's just all feeling really overwhelming. Some days, I feel like I'm barely holding it together. I'll be trying to get everything done, and then the baby will need a diaper change, or she'll start crying, and it's just like... everything falls apart.

And it's not just the baby stuff, either. It's like, everything else in my life is still going on, too. I've got to keep the house clean, and cook meals, and take care of myself... and it's just feeling like too much. I'll be trying to do one thing, and then I'll think, "Oh, I need to do this other thing, too," and it's just like... my brain gets overwhelmed.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeling like I'm doing okay, and then suddenly I'll think about all the things I need to do, and it's like... this wave of exhaustion will just wash over me. I'll be like, "How am I going to get all this done? How am I going to take care of the baby and myself and the house and everything else?" And it's just feeling really, really overwhelming.

My husband tries to help, but even with his help, it's just feeling like too much. I'll be like, "I don't know how to do this," and he'll be like, "You're doing great," but it's hard to believe him when I'm feeling so overwhelmed. It's like, I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually living my life. And that's a really hard feeling to deal with.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah... that's been happening to me a lot lately. I'll be lying in bed, trying to sleep, and my mind will just start racing. I'll think about the baby, and whether she's okay, and whether I'm doing everything right. And then I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, and how I'm going to get everything done. And it's just like... my brain won't turn off.

Sometimes, I'll be so worried about something that I'll get out of bed and go check on the baby, just to make sure she's okay. And then I'll be awake for hours, just lying there, thinking about everything that could go wrong. It's like, my mind is just constantly racing, and I don't know how to calm it down.

And even when I'm not thinking about specific things, I just feel... anxious, I guess. Like, I'll be lying there, feeling restless and uneasy, and I won't know why. It's like, my body is just tense, and I don't know how to relax.

I've been trying to establish a bedtime routine, and get some exercise during the day, and all that stuff, but it's just not working. I'll be tired, but I won't be able to sleep. Or, I'll fall asleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I won't be able to go back to sleep.

It's hard, because I know I need sleep to take care of the baby, and to take care of myself. But it's just... my mind won't cooperate, I guess. And it's frustrating, because I feel like I'm not doing anything right, and that I'm just failing at everything.

Sometimes, my husband will try to help me relax, and he'll be like, "Just breathe, and try to calm down," but it's hard to do that when my mind is racing. And it's not like I'm not trying... it's just... I don't know, it's like my brain is just wired to worry, or something.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah... I'd say that's been happening to me a lot lately. I mean, I'm happy to have my baby, and I love her so much, but at the same time, I just feel... sad, I guess. It's like, I'm supposed to be this happy, new mom, but really, I'm just feeling overwhelmed and anxious all the time.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. And it's not even like I'm thinking about anything specific, it's just... this feeling of sadness will just wash over me. And it's hard, because I don't know how to explain it to my husband, or to my friends and family. They're all like, "Oh, you're just tired, you're just adjusting to motherhood," but it's more than that.

I feel like I'm losing myself, or something. Like, I used to be this person who was happy and carefree, and now I'm just this anxious, worried person all the time. And it's hard to see my friends and family, because they all seem so happy and put together, and I just feel like... I don't know, like I'm just barely holding on, I guess.

Sometimes, I'll have a good day, and I'll think, "Okay, maybe I'm finally getting the hang of this," but then the next day will be hard again, and I'll feel like I'm right back where I started. It's like, I'm just on this rollercoaster of emotions, and I don't know how to get off.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be grateful for my baby, and I am, I really am. But at the same time, I just feel... sad, and overwhelmed, and like I'm not doing anything right. And it's hard to talk about, because I don't want to seem like I'm not grateful for my baby, or like I'm not happy to be a mom. But at the same time, I need to be honest about how I'm feeling, because I don't know how to make it stop.
